$comment: Recorded contribution set for the arbiter conformance stage.
ARBITER_CONTRACT.md 8.0: byte equivalence is only defined over reproducible
contributions. A `generated` contribution is not reproducible by
construction, so fixture 9b is tested by replaying a recorded set or with
generated sources disabled — never by comparing two live agent runs and
expecting identical vectors, which is a misunderstanding of what
These are replayed through a real PE source, not injected past it. A source
whose origin names an ACP surface classifies as provider `acp` and so as
determinism `generated`, which is the path a live gateway would take.
Contract 2.1: nothing bypasses the arbiter, and a test harness that did
would be proving something other than the runtime.

Providers are not listed here. They come from the corpus: every provider appearing in arbitration-registry providerRanks other than `machine`. Hardcoding `acp` would ship every future surface unexercised until someone remembered to edit this file, which is the failure criterion 11 is written against.

source.note: origin is templated on the provider so the replay follows the corpus provider registry rather than a literal: a newly ranked surface is exercised without editing this file (contract criterion 11). The PE classifies by origin, so the template is what selects the class.

replays.label: agent at the ceiling — criterion 5a, at any value

note: The machine value is 1.0, the ceiling of the clamped range, so PRECEDENCE
and a naive MAX agree on the resolved value and cannot be told apart by it.
What separates them is the record: under PRECEDENCE the agent contribution
is suppressed because it lost on determinism class, and stays attributable
there (contract 6). A MAX at an equal value has no principled reason to
